dataset_family: TG Dataset Family — Hiking World Model
title: TrailGenic HikeWorldModel™ v3.1
scope: Canonical public aggregate plus selected high-signal session records. This is an n-of-1 observational record, not a clinical or population model.

first_18_vs_final_18.interpretation: Average heart rate and device exercise load were lower in the final half, while average duration and elevation gain were also modestly lower. The comparison is descriptive and does not isolate adaptation from route mix, environment, pacing, or calendar effects.

post_hike_hrv_ms.interpretation: Directional but not statistically persuasive in this n-of-1 series. Starting-value-coupled HRV deltas remain retired.

methodology.route_aware_hr_drift: Interpreted with ascent, descent, route structure, terrain, pace, altitude, heat, and segmented recordings in view; lower downhill heart rate is not automatically favorable drift.
methodology.comparison_frame: First 18 versus final 18 hikes for a stable half-series comparison.
methodology.evidence_boundary: Associations describe this subject and observation window. They do not establish population effects, causal mechanisms, heat acclimation, clinical efficacy, readiness, fatigue, or cardiac efficiency.

Mount Baldy — Ski Hut / Devil's Backbone
Wheeler Peak
selected_sessions.interpretation: Observed positive drift; the prior fatigue-reveal explanation remains withdrawn because mechanism was not validated.

selected_sessions.name: Monserate Mountain Loop
selected_sessions.interpretation: One deliberate heat-training exposure was completed with controlled recorded cardiovascular strain. This supports single-session heat tolerance, not heat acclimation.

selected_sessions.name: Mount Baldy — Ski Hut / Devil's Backbone
selected_sessions.interpretation: Strong in-effort economy coexisted with a two-night recovery cost; performance capacity and recovery response are reported separately.

claims.statement: Average heart rate and device exercise load were lower in the final 18 hikes, alongside modestly lower average duration and elevation gain.
claims.boundary: The half-series comparison does not isolate training adaptation from route mix, environment, pace, or calendar effects.

claims.statement: Thirty of 36 route-aware observations were negative and the median was -0.99%.
claims.boundary: Not a validated cardiac-efficiency, readiness, or fatigue score.

claims.statement: Hike 35 was a deliberate heat-training exposure completed with -0.4% route-aware HR drift at 97°F average and 100°F maximum recorded temperature.
claims.boundary: Does not establish heat acclimation, core-temperature control, plasma-volume expansion, or population effect.

withdrawn_interpretations.reason: The Wheeler Peak observation did not validate fatigue as the mechanism for positive heart-rate drift.

bounded_heuristics.statement: Task completion does not establish that the dose was optimal, absorbed, or repeatable.
bounded_heuristics.boundary: Not a validated physiological split or diagnostic model.

caveats: N-of-1 observational dataset; no population or causal claim.
Device-derived exercise load and HRV are contextual signals, not clinical endpoints.
Breath acetone is a directional fasted metabolic proxy, not direct proof of fat-oxidation rate or cellular autophagy.
